semantic_method: Read all 66 original baseline PDF pages, inspect selected rendered ambiguity pages, manually group by meaning, retain prose permissions and exceptions, and mechanically reproduce indexed quotations.
quotation_policy: Exact indexed text with indexed normalization/correction policy; raw extraction stays in source_index.jsonl. Every period is an extraction boundary, including abbreviations and section numbers.
proof_policy: One proposed encompassing top-level Lean theorem per group. No Lean code or proofs are constructed.
force_policy: T=O is required when applicable; Threshold/Objective alternatives are choices; Optional objectives are not universally mandatory; unlabeled prose retains its own wording and may impose obligations.
definitions_policy: Context passages and Appendix A background units remain shared references; quoted descriptive clauses do not become unconditional mandates merely because they occur in a group.

groups.title: Two independent encryption layers and allowed tunnel pairings

requirement_passages.text: The MSC Solution uses two nested, independent encryption tunnels to protect the confidentiality and integrity of data as it transits the untrusted network.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: The two encryption tunnels protecting a data flow can use either Internet Protocol Security (IPsec) generated by a Virtual Private Network (VPN) Gateway or Media Access Control Security (MACsec) generated by a MACsec Device.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: VPN Gateways and MACsec Devices are implemented as part of the network infrastructure.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: Throughout this CP, the term “Encryption Component” refers generically to either a VPN Gateway or a MACsec Device.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: “Inner Encryption Component” refers to the component that terminates the Inner layer of encryption and “Outer Encryption Component” refers to the component that terminates the Outer layer of encryption.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: As shown in Figure 1, before being sent across the untrusted network, each packet or frame of classified data is encrypted twice; first by an Inner Encryption Component, and then by an Outer Encryption Component.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: At the other end of the data flow, the received packet is correspondingly decrypted twice; first by an Outer Encryption Component, and then by an Inner Encryption Component.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: Data plane traffic is classified information, encrypted or unencrypted, that passes through the MSC Solution.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: The MSC Solution exists to encrypt and decrypt data plane traffic.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: All data plane traffic within the Gray and Black Networks is encapsulated within the IPsec’s Encapsulating Security Payload (ESP) and/or MACsec protocols.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: There are two layers of encryption tunnels between any pair of sites communicating directly with one another; one encryption tunnel between their Outer Encryption Components, and a second encryption tunnel between their Inner Encryption Components.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: Each set of Inner or Outer Encryption Components can provide encryption using either IPsec or MACsec.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: Each layer of the MSC Solution can use either an IPsec tunnel or MACsec tunnel.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: An IPsec tunnel is established between VPN Gateways.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: A MACsec tunnel is established between MACsec Devices.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: For configurations 2 and 4 which use an outer MACsec tunnel these solutions would only be point to point solutions instead of a multi-site solution.

groups.title: Connectivity restricted to the same security level

requirement_passages.text: This CP describes a general MSC Solution to protect classified information as it travels across either an untrusted Network, or a different security level network.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: The solution supports interconnecting two or more networks operating at the same security level via encryption tunnels, where the security level encompasses the classification level, list of compartments, dissemination controls, and other such controls over information.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: The solution provides sufficient flexibility to be applicable to many use cases of MSC implementations.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: The Red Network is logically located behind an Inner Encryption Component.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: The networks connected to one another through the MSC Solution are Red Networks.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: Red Networks may only communicate with one another through the MSC Solution if the networks operate at the same security level.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: A single implementation of the MSC Solution may support Red Networks of different security levels.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: The MSC Solution provides secure connectivity between the Red Networks within each security level while preventing Red Networks of different security levels from communicating with one another.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: This enables a customer to use the same physical infrastructure to carry traffic from multiple networks.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: Although each Red Network requires its own Inner Encryption Component, a site may use a single Outer Encryption Component to encrypt and transport traffic that has been encrypted by Inner Encryption Components of varying security levels.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: There is no limit to the number of different security levels that an MSC Solution may support.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: An unclassified network can also be included behind the Outer Encryption Component but must be behind its own Inner Encryption Component and meet the requirements in this CP as if it was a Red Network.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: A single implementation of the MSC Solution may support Red Networks of different security levels, to include unclassified networks.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: If Certification Authorities (CAs) are part of the MSC Solution, each site has the option to use either locally run CAs that they manage and control or, where available, enterprise CAs that are not necessarily managed by the Solution Owner.

groups.title: MACsec encapsulation and standalone encapsulator obligations

requirement_passages.text: The MACsec-encrypted traffic needs to be encapsulated if the MACsec Device is the first layer of encryption in the MSC Solution or if the MACsec-encrypted traffic needs to traverse an IP-based network.

requirement_passages.text: Encapsulation creates a new packet by adding a new header, and sometimes trailer, to the MACsec-encrypted traffic.

requirement_passages.text: Encapsulation ensures the MACsec-encrypted traffic is not decrypted prior to reaching its destination and ensures the second layer of encryption can be applied.

requirement_passages.text: In some commercial MACsec Devices, encapsulation can be applied on the internal interface by creating a pseudowire (see Figure 7), which emulates a point-to-point connection.

requirement_passages.text: If this feature is not supported, a standalone device is needed to encapsulate the MACsec-encrypted data (see Figure 8).

requirement_passages.text: If using a standalone device, the internal interface will be connected to the Inner MACsec Device and the external interface will be connected to the Outer Encryption Component.

requirement_passages.text: 0 is relevant to the choice of cryptography employed in IPsec and especially affects the Internet Key Exchange Protocol Version 2 (IKEv2) key establishment construction, requiring support for several new RFCs.

requirement_passages.text: 0-compliant algorithms ML-KEM-1024 [FIPS203] for key establishment and ML-DSA-87 [FIPS204] for digital signatures within IPsec.

requirement_passages.text: It describes the use of RFCs that are required in order to support the large ML- KEM-1024 public key and ciphertext sizes, including:
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: • RFC 7383 IKEv2 Message Fragmentation
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: • RFC 9242 Intermediate Key Exchanges in IKEv2
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: • RFC 9370 Multiple Key Exchanges in IKEv2
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: • draft-ietf-ipsecme-ikev2-pqc-auth Signature Authentication in the IKEv2 using PQC
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: • RFC 9881 Internet X.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: 509 Public Key Infrastructure - Algorithm Identifiers for the Module-Lattice- Based Digital Signature Algorithm (ML-DSA)
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: • draft-ietf-ipsecme-ikev2-mlkem Post-quantum Key Exchange with ML-KEM in the IKEv2
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: These additional RFCs facilitate the use of ML-KEM-1024 without causing IP-level fragmentation, which can create operational challenges and prevent the establishment of a connection.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: In particular, if ML- KEM-1024 were used in the initial IKEv2 Security Association (SA) key exchange (IKE_SA_INIT), the sizes of its public key and ciphertext would cause the initiator and responder messages to exceed the typical path Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) and necessitate IP-level fragmentation.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: In order to prevent this issue, the solution leveraged first performs a CNSA 1.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: 0-compliant key establishment that does not exceed PMTU and subsequently performs an additional key establishment using a newly-defined exchange called Intermediate Exchange (IKE_INTERMEDIATE).
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: IKE_INTERMEDIATE exchanges can circumvent IP-level fragmentation by using IKEv2-level fragmentation, which does not incur the same operational issues.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: The specifications of which this solution is comprised work as follows:
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: RFC 7383 IKEv2 Fragmentation: Describes a way to prevent IP fragmentation of large encrypted IKEv2 messages by fragmenting at the IKEv2 layer.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: This allows IKEv2 messages to traverse network devices that do not allow IP fragments to pass through.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: RFC 9242 Intermediate Key Exchanges: Specifies a new exchange type called IKE_INTERMEDIATE.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: IKE_INTERMEDIATE exchanges can be used for transferring large amounts of data in the process of establishing an IKEv2 Security Association.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: It is sent after IKE_SA_INIT and before IKE_AUTH.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: RFC 9370 Multiple Key Exchanges: Leverages the IKE_INTERMEDIATE exchange specified in RFC 9242 in order to perform multiple key establishments.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: In particular, this document enables the use of a quantum resistant key establishment algorithm whose public key and ciphertexts would exceed MTU and cause IP fragmentation of the IKE_SA_INIT messages.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: The document resolves this issue by specifying how to perform such large key establishments in IKE_INTERMEDIATE which can benefit from the IKEv2 fragmentation mechanism specified in RFC 7383.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: An initial key establishment that does not cause IP fragmentation is first performed in IKE_SA_INIT, followed by additional key establishment(s) using IKE_INTERMEDIATE message(s).
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: As detailed in Figure 10, RFC 9370 enables peers to perform multiple key exchanges.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: The key- establishment algorithm used in the Initial IKE SA (IKE_SA_INIT) exchange must be constrained enough in size as to not induce IP fragmentation.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: The ML-KEM-1024 public key and ciphertext sizes are too large for this initial exchange and thus the IKE_SA_INIT exchange must use a CNSA 1.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: 0-compliant key establishment algorithm.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: A subsequent Intermediate IKE (IKE_INTERMEDIATE) exchange (as specified in RFC 9242) is then used to perform an ML-KEM key establishment.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: This second exchange, encrypted using keys established by IKE_SA_INIT, can leverage the IKEv2-level fragmentation mechanism specified in RFC 7383.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: • The customer’s testing team develops a test plan and performs testing of the MSC Solution (see Section 13.

requirement_passages.text: This section provides a framework for a Test and Evaluation (T&E) plan and procedures to validate the implementation of an MSC Solution.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: T&E is a critical part of the approval process for the AO, providing a robust body of evidence that shows compliance with this CP.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: The security features and operational capabilities associated with the use of the solution must be tested.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: The following is a general high-level methodology for developing the T&E plan and procedures and for the execution of those procedures to validate the implementation and functionality of the MSC Solution.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: The entire solution, to include each component described in Section 5, is addressed by this test plan, including the following:
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: 1) Set up the baseline network and configure all components.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: 2) Document the baseline network configuration.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: Include product model and serial numbers, software version numbers, and software configuration settings, at a minimum.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: 3) Develop a test plan for the specific implementation using the test requirements from the MSC CP Testing Annex.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: Any additional requirements imposed by the local AO should also be tested, and the test plan must include tests to ensure that these requirements do not interfere with the security of this solution as described in this CP.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: 4) Perform testing using the test plan derived in Step 3.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: Network testing will consist of both Black Box testing and Gray Box testing.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: A two-person testing approach should be used to administer the tests.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: During test execution, security and non-security related discrepancies with the solution must be documented.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: 5) Compile findings, to include comments and vulnerability details as well as possible countermeasure information, into a Final Test Report to be delivered to the AO for approval of the solution.
requirement_passages.quotation_basis: Exact indexed text; only documented source-index whitespace normalization and corrections apply.

requirement_passages.text: There are two outer encryption tunnels that transit the Black Network: one between the upper pair of Outer Encryption Components, and one between the lower pair of Outer Encryption Components.

open_issues.title: Standalone encapsulator boundary and requirement strength conflict
open_issues.detail: §4.2.3 and §5.5 require all Solution Component obligations; below Figure 8 the encapsulation step is outside the solution with DM/PF highly recommended; MD-13 mandates §11.1 treatment. Resolve applicability without silently deleting any passage.

open_issues.title: Same-level filtering sentence conflicts with the permitted peers
open_issues.detail: §5.2 says to prevent same-security-level communication. Other provisions allow same-level tunnels and prohibit different-level communication. The original words remain uncorrected.

open_issues.title: Management encryption and local exceptions
open_issues.detail: Broad two-layer Gray-management wording coexists with direct physical-management exceptions, LAN/VLAN qualification, and a same-site CNSA exemption. The scope of each exception needs a formal applicability decision.

open_issues.title: TRANSEC requirement strength and applicability differ
open_issues.detail: Public-Internet prose says must, while OR-9 is Objective for MACsec connected to an Outer Firewall and has a blank Alternatives cell.

open_issues.title: New-version compliance deadline conflict
open_issues.detail: §13.3 specifies six months from notification; GD-11 specifies the next registration renewal. No precedence is supplied.

open_issues.title: AS connection scope wording
open_issues.detail: The prose says AS must not connect to both Gray and/or Red Networks; AA-2 says only one site’s network. Network/layer/site cardinality needs a source-faithful formal definition.

open_issues.title: Gray address-only restrictions and explicit non-tunnel exceptions
open_issues.detail: Only-peer-address rules must be interpreted with the separately enumerated management/control/revocation allowances; blindly conjoining unqualified allowlists would lose allowed traffic.

open_issues.title: Objective table row has no Alternative marker
open_issues.detail: PF-10 is Objective with a blank Alternatives cell despite §8.1 describing optional objectives as marked Optional. Preserve the blank and seek review.

open_issues.title: MACsec provisioning paragraph uses VPN terminology
open_issues.detail: The certificate-based MACsec paragraph names the Inner VPN Gateway CSR. Do not silently correct the quotation; identify the intended device in later formalization.

open_issues.title: External annex dependencies are not supplied
open_issues.detail: Key management, symmetric key management, continuous monitoring, enterprise Gray implementation, and testing annex contents are outside the supplied PDF. Relocation markers are preserved in background, with referents; their substantive obligations cannot be recovered here.

open_issues.title: EAP-TLS CAK derivation and blanket KGS generation wording
open_issues.detail: The authentication prose derives a CAK from the EAP-TLS MSK, then says all CAKs and CKNs must be generated by an NSA-approved KGS. The applicability of the KGS requirement to the certificate-derived branch must be resolved without changing either quotation.

evidence_scope_notes.title: Figures and protocol examples do not prove compliance
evidence_scope_notes.detail: Figures and protocol examples support source-grounded, clause-specific requirement assessments. Implementation tests and theorem proofs require later evidence and models. That ordinary evidence boundary does not prevent extracting the requirements illustrated by an example.

domain_review_scope.title: Legal-domain interpretation remains unreviewed
domain_review_scope.detail: The legal undertaking is retained as a non-network obligation. Its formal applicability and any legal meaning need dedicated review; the extraction makes no enforceability claim.

resolved_interpretations.title: AW host and VM restrictions apply together
resolved_interpretations.detail: §6.2 prohibits the AW host from hosting enrollment/provisioning/registration/SIEM VMs. DM-24 refers to separate workstations or VMs. The host-level scope must remain visible.
resolved_interpretations.resolution: Separate service VMs must also respect the AW host restriction. Distinct VMs do not authorize provisioning, enrollment, registration, or SIEM VMs on an AW-dedicated host.

resolved_interpretations.title: Physical, cryptographic, and ACL separation apply together
resolved_interpretations.detail: §4.1.4 requires physical and cryptographic data/management separation and says VLAN alone is insufficient; DM-25 states at least logical separation by Gray Firewall ACL. Retain both requirements.
resolved_interpretations.resolution: The minimum logical separation required by DM-25 does not waive the physical and cryptographic separation in §4.1.4. The conditions can be imposed together.
